prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Official domains: warbyparker.com
Recipient: the marketing team
Packet status: ok

Evidence passages:
[P1] source: https://www.warbyparker.com/impact-report | document: official_domain | type: historical_activity | dates in text: 2025 | published: unknown
"Community To date, our Buy a Pair, Give a Pair program has served individuals in more than 80 countries and provided over 25 million pairs of glasses to people in need. In 2025, we launched a collaboration with Bloomberg Philanthropies that will enable the distribution of glasses to millions more people in need worldwide—and double the impact of our Pupils Project in select cities, providing free eye exams and glasses to students around the United States. Two young Buddhist monks smile at the camera. They are wearing traditional maroon robes over hoodies."

[P2] source: https://www.warbyparker.com/impact-report | document: official_domain | type: historical_activity | flags: forward_looking_statement | dates in text: 2025 | published: unknown
"Customers Each and every day, our team aims to create high-quality products and deliver remarkable experiences that delight our more than two million customers. In 2025, we launched Advisor, a first-of-its-kind tool that makes tailored product recommendations based on a customer’s facial measurements and style preferences. We also announced a landmark partnership with Google and Samsung to develop AI-powered glasses for all-day wear, providing customers with instant context and insight as they navigate the world. A snapshot of 2025: 3 new lens types, 88% of stores offer eye exams, and 33 million+ lives covered. Two men look at glasses in a store."

[P3] source: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/warby-parker-barker-13-other-brilliant-instagram-from-bollinger | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"5. Find Creative Ways to Collaborate with Like-Minded Influencers Collaborating with influential Instagrammers is a great way to reach out to their gigantic fan-base. This is why most brands incorporate this strategy in their social marketing plans. Warby Parker gives its own little twist to influential marketing and has collaborated with:"

[P4] source: https://sadiemattson.wordpress.com/2026/02/15/how-warby-parker-used-strategic-social-media-to-reinvent-eyewear/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: 2010, 2017 | published: unknown
"Social Media as Community, Not Just Promotion Instead of only using social media to promote their brand, Warby Parker treats platforms such as Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, and YouTube as places for real conversations and engagement (Mahoney & Tang, 2017). The company encourages customers to share their photos, experiences, and feedback, making user-generated content a key part of their marketing strategy (Kaplan & Haenlein, 2010). This can be seen through Warby Parker’s Home Try-On program. It encourages people to share photos and opinions online intentionally. This strategy has turned customers into contributors and has helped spread the word naturally through recommendations from friends."

[P5] source: https://www.latterly.org/warby-parker-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Influencer Partnerships and Community Engagement Social proof shapes fashion and health decisions, especially for products that must fit faces and budgets. Warby Parker blends creator collaborations with service-led community programs that build credibility. The approach turns authentic endorsements and local activations into measurable demand. Creators supply style context and fit validation, while community outreach demonstrates care, access, and impact. Together they raise awareness, generate UGC, and broaden reach beyond paid impressions. The halo from mission work supports long-term loyalty and favorable word of mouth."

[P6] source: https://www.latterly.org/warby-parker-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Buy a Pair, Give a Pair collaborations with VisionSpring and partners, surpassing 15 million pairs distributed and expanding access to vision care. * Mobile screenings and local events, offering basic exams and education, then directing patients to affordable solutions and nearby stores. * Campus ambassador initiatives that promote Home Try-On, student discounts, and exam bookings during peak academic periods. * Neighborhood pop-ups featuring adjustments and quick repairs, creating goodwill and generating referral volume. Warby Parker turns influence and community into a unified trust engine that feeds both brand strength and sales."

[P7] source: https://investors.warbyparker.com/overview/ | document: official_domain | type: historical_activity | flags: forward_looking_statement | dates in text: 2010 | published: unknown
"About Us Warby Parker was founded with a mission: to inspire and impact the world with vision, purpose, and style. We aim to demonstrate that a business can scale, become profitable, and do good in the world—without charging a premium for it. Since the day we launched in 2010, we’ve pioneered ideas, designed products, and developed technologies that help people see—from designer-quality prescription glasses (starting at $95) and contacts to eye exams and vision tests. Customers can meet us online, at more than 300 Warby Parker stores across the U.S. and Canada, or even in their home."

[P8] source: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/warby-parker-barker-13-other-brilliant-instagram-from-bollinger | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"And finally, they partnered with professional storm catchers (I didn’t know they existed either!) and produced visually stunning pictures of the eclipse: The best bit? It was one of the very few optical brands that used this event creatively and successfully. Others opted for a meh description of the eclipse and some do’s and don’ts. * NYC marathon Warby Parker encouraged NYC marathon runners by giving away super-cute finisher pins at their NYC stores. This was a clever marketing move as lots of people tagged marathon runners they knew so that they could grab a pin too. This way, Warby Parker reached their followers’ friends (and friends of friends)."

[P9] source: https://sadiemattson.wordpress.com/2026/02/15/how-warby-parker-used-strategic-social-media-to-reinvent-eyewear/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: 2010, 2017 | published: unknown
"A Fresh Take on Eyewear Founded in 2010, Warby Parker shook up an industry that was known for its high prices and lack of customer engagement (Mahoney & Tang, 2017). Instead of sticking to the usual retail methods, the company took advantage of digital platforms to connect directly with customers and share a brand story that focuses on being accessible, open, and socially responsible (Mahoney & Tang, 2017). Warby Parker did not just sell glasses, but changed the eyewear game by showing brands a new way to connect with their customers through smart social media and community-focused marketing (Mahoney & Tang, 2017)."

[P10] source: https://sadiemattson.wordpress.com/2026/02/15/how-warby-parker-used-strategic-social-media-to-reinvent-eyewear/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: 2010, 2017 | published: unknown
"Why This Still Matters Today Warby Parker understood social media marketing strategies early, which are now the norm. Way before influencer tools and analytics were everywhere, Warby Parker focused on authenticity, engaging with their audience, and building a community (Mahoney & Tang, 2017). Even with social media getting increasingly driven by algorithms and competition, the main takeaway stays the same. Brands that listen, interact, and encourage participation usually create stronger connections and lasting influence (Kaplan & Haenlein, 2010)."
